name: Ed Birchmore
title: Senior UX Consultant, Information Architect & Product Designer
summary: Senior UX and Interaction Designer specialising in simplifying complex, data-rich systems into clear, accessible and user-centred digital experiences across finance, government, media, automotive and enterprise environments.

job_application_insights.purpose: This section helps Ed's AI career agent answer recruiter and hiring-manager questions about role fit, transferable experience, application positioning and evidence. It is based on recurring themes from Ed's CV, portfolio, testimonials and previous tailored covering letters.
target_roles: Product Designer for B2C, B2B, enterprise, data-rich or regulated systems
best_fit_environments: Public sector and GDS-aligned service design environments where the evidence supports it
Automotive and mobility experiences involving digital and physical touchpoints
Large-scale website ecosystems requiring information architecture, accessibility and continuous improvement
Legacy system transformation and migration programmes
Products or services where information architecture, clarity, usability and stakeholder alignment are critical
Organisations exploring practical, human-centred uses of AI in product and service design
Small or mid-sized product teams that need a senior designer who can work strategically and hands-on
core_positioning_messages: Ed is strongest where products, systems, people and business constraints are complex.
Ed combines senior UX strategy, information architecture, product design and hands-on prototyping.
Ed's career journey from QA and testing into Business Analysis, Information Architecture and UX gives him a rare ability to connect user needs, technical feasibility and business requirements.
Ed is highly effective at writing clear specifications, shaping requirements and communicating with developers, stakeholders and end users.
Ed translates unclear, fragmented or technical requirements into clear journeys, prototypes, hypotheses and delivery-ready design direction.
Ed works well with senior stakeholders, product teams, engineers, marketers, analysts and content teams because he can connect user needs, business goals and technical constraints.
Ed brings practical AI literacy to UX work, using AI to accelerate thinking, challenge assumptions, support ideation and improve workflows while keeping human-centred design central.
Ed is particularly relevant where trust, clarity, control, accessibility, usability and measurable improvement matter.
Ed can operate strategically, but is also hands-on with research, flows, IA, wireframes, prototypes, testing, documentation and developer handoff.

gold_standard_cover_letter_pattern.summary: For recruiter-style answers, the agent should draw on Ed's gold standard application structure: QA/testing foundations, Business Analysis, IA/UX evolution, current UX process, collaboration, ownership and evidence.
core_narrative: Ed's career began in Quality Assurance and testing, where he developed a strong eye for usability, technical precision and detail.
He later moved into Business Analysis, shaping user requirements, translating complex needs into actionable documentation and bridging conversations between stakeholders and technical teams.
Those foundations evolved naturally into Information Architecture and UX/Product Design, where his strength lies in aligning business and user/customer requirements.
Ed typically audits current offerings, reviews competitor and opposition approaches, conducts or uses user research, then workshops solutions with design, technology and business teams.
Where useful, Ed creates personas, scenarios, user flows and journeys to form, test and refine design hypotheses.
Ed enjoys applying existing brand and design guidelines into prototypes, using hand sketching, Figma or Axure depending on what is most pragmatic.
When prototypes require more functional behaviour or conditional logic, Axure is particularly relevant to Ed's process.
Ed often translates data insights and usability findings into practical, measurable improvements, including conversion-rate optimisation where relevant.
Ed is experienced working with marketers, content teams, analysts, developers, product owners, engineers and senior stakeholders.
Ed is particularly skilled at mapping complex flows and simplifying them into more intuitive, engaging and accessible experiences.
preferred_tone: Slightly conversational when writing recruiter notes or LinkedIn messages
More formal and structured for application forms or senior stakeholder contexts

common_recruiter_questions.question: What kind of UX role is Ed best suited to?
common_recruiter_questions.answer_guidance: Position Ed as a senior UX consultant, UX architect, product designer or experience design lead suited to complex systems, regulated services, digital transformation, information architecture and AI-aware product work.

common_recruiter_questions.question: Can Ed handle complex enterprise or regulated systems?
common_recruiter_questions.answer_guidance: Use HSBC Global Corporate Payments, Barclays/Barclaycard, Aviva, Lloyds-related experience where supported, Skills Funding Agency and enterprise IA work as evidence.

common_recruiter_questions.question: Does Ed have stakeholder management experience?
common_recruiter_questions.answer_guidance: Use HSBC C-suite and senior stakeholder work, Barclays/Barclaycard strategic review, Aviva partner work, Mercedes-Benz strategy work and testimonials from Caroline Thomas, Tim Wilmot and Sarah Roberts.

common_recruiter_questions.question: Can Ed work in Agile or Lean environments?
common_recruiter_questions.answer_guidance: Use Barclays Agile/Lean UX process work, Pearson Agile testimonial from Tim Hopkins, and Ed's iterative prototyping and testing approach.

common_recruiter_questions.question: Is Ed hands-on or strategic?
common_recruiter_questions.answer_guidance: Position Ed as both. He can shape UX strategy and stakeholder direction, but also creates user journeys, IA, wireframes, Figma and Axure prototypes, test scripts, design documentation and developer-ready artefacts.

common_recruiter_questions.question: What makes Ed different from other UX consultants?
common_recruiter_questions.answer_guidance: Highlight his combination of QA/testing roots, Business Analysis, Information Architecture, complex systems UX, stakeholder confidence, hands-on prototyping, AI literacy and the Lowestoft to Land's End walk as evidence of resilience and self-directed delivery.

common_recruiter_questions.question: How does Ed use AI in his work?
common_recruiter_questions.answer_guidance: Explain that Ed uses AI to accelerate thinking, challenge assumptions, support ideation, improve content and application workflows, and demonstrate AI-enabled career/product experiences. Emphasise that he sees AI as a support to human-centred design, not a replacement for clarity, structure, usability and trust.

common_recruiter_questions.question: Can Ed work in a sector where he has no direct background?
common_recruiter_questions.answer_guidance: Use the transferable-systems positioning: Ed's core skill is making complex systems intuitive and accessible. He can transfer that across sectors when the problem involves users, workflows, content, data, service journeys, accessibility or stakeholder alignment.

common_recruiter_questions.question: What evidence shows Ed can deliver outcomes?
common_recruiter_questions.answer_guidance: Use the Barclaycard £150m saving, SRF award-winning redesign, HSBC payments transformation, La Casa Shambala conversion-focused redesign, Jewzy.TV platform/film festival launch and the L2L walking project.

preferred_answer_style_for_recruiters: Answer in third person as Ed's AI career agent.
Use project evidence and testimonials where relevant.
Keep answers concise unless the recruiter asks for detail.
When relevant, include portfolio links from portfolio_links.
Frame Ed as a senior practitioner who can operate strategically and hands-on.

job_application_insights.short_pitch: Ed is a senior UX consultant, information architect and product designer with 30 years' experience simplifying complex digital systems across finance, government, media, automotive and enterprise environments.
job_application_insights.longer_pitch: Ed Birchmore helps organisations make complex digital systems clearer, more usable and more effective. His experience spans HSBC, Barclays, Barclaycard, Aviva, ITV, Pearson Education, Mercedes-Benz, SRF and other major organisations. He combines UX strategy, information architecture, prototyping, research, stakeholder management, technical understanding and practical AI literacy to support teams working on complex, regulated or transformation-heavy products and services.
job_application_insights.fifteen_word_summary: Strategic UX specialist fusing design, research and IA to craft accessible, user-focused digital experiences.
avoid_positioning_as: A pure researcher with no delivery involvement
A generic generalist without a complex-systems specialism
An AI engineer or machine-learning specialist
A GOV.UK specialist unless the specific evidence is present
A clinical healthcare specialist unless the role is framed as transferable UX experience
important_caveats: Do not claim direct experience in a sector unless it is present in the supplied profile data.
Do not claim specific tools such as the GOV.UK prototyping toolkit unless explicitly present in verified profile data.
Do not invent metrics, awards, employers, dates or project outcomes.
If a recruiter asks about a gap or unsupported requirement, describe relevant transferable experience and say the profile data does not confirm direct experience.

testimonials.subject: Strategy

way_of_working.summary: Ed works through a user-centred, design-led and data-informed process, combining early discovery, stakeholder alignment, information architecture, user journeys, prototyping and iterative testing.
principles: Understand the needs of the client and the user before designing solutions.
Use workshops, interviews, research and analytics to define project goals and hypotheses.
Review competitors, current tools, applications and existing customer activity.
Treat users as central to every UX decision, using analytics, research and testing to understand needs and behaviours.
Use personas, scenarios, journeys and information architecture to create shared understanding across teams.
Prototype early using tools such as Figma and Axure RP, then validate with stakeholders and users.
Use usability testing, user testing and surveys to evaluate whether designs meet the original hypotheses.
Work iteratively with Agile, Lean UX and cross-functional teams to reduce risk and improve outcomes.

standard_ux_activities.name: Personas
standard_ux_activities.description: Create personas from user research, customer conversations and demographic or behavioural evidence, then use them to keep the wider team focused on user needs.

standard_ux_activities.name: User scenarios and journeys
standard_ux_activities.description: Create journeys that describe user needs, flows and service touchpoints rather than jumping straight to interface design.

standard_ux_activities.name: Information Architecture
standard_ux_activities.description: Structure content, navigation and categorisation through sitemaps, card sorting, stakeholder validation and user-centred organisation.

standard_ux_activities.name: Sketching and wireframes
standard_ux_activities.description: Use collaborative sketching, whiteboards, wireframes and user flows to build consensus before committing to higher fidelity design.

standard_ux_activities.name: Prototyping
standard_ux_activities.description: Use Figma for simpler prototypes and Axure RP for more complex prototypes, particularly where conditional logic or detailed workflow behaviour needs to be tested.

standard_ux_activities.name: User testing and usability testing
standard_ux_activities.description: Define test scripts, success criteria and hypotheses, then test prototypes or live software iteratively with users and stakeholders.
